title: Optimal Cause-Blind Current-Status Survey Design for Cumulative-Incidence Contrasts

The claimed novelty relative to Jewell–van der Laan–Shiboski remains unverified because the direct antecedent's theorem text was unavailable; that source comparison must be completed before asserting that continuous sensitivity optimality and attainment are new rather than an application or extension of its monitoring-design theory.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery produced a D0 core with the known-censoring mixed-source efficiency bound, global design certificate, certified approximation, pilot oracle-value attainment, and conditional efficient inference. D0.5 graded the delivered package subfield because its paper-score ceiling was 7.1 below the 7.4 field floor; formalization did not start. The closest Jewell–van der Laan–Shiboski theorem text could not be inspected because publisher access was denied, so this entry claims no priority over it.
tldr: A positive-fraction cause-labeled cohort makes the randomized cause-1 cumulative-incidence contrast regularly estimable, while a cause-blind current-status survey can reduce timing variance. All information calculations use the identifiable administrative quotient that collapses \(T_a>\tau\) to one unmarked survivor state, leaving the observed law and the target at \(t^\star<\tau\) unchanged. The paper derives the marked mixed-source efficient variance, proves a necessary-and-sufficient global sensitivity certificate, and supplies a terminating finite rational, support-aware quotient-Galerkin, and interval-quadrature certificate. An independent pilot uses a bounded IPW survivor-mass estimate and the threshold \(m_n^{-1/4}\) to choose the fitted survivor coordinate operationally, then selects an atomic design attaining oracle value and supports efficient conditional inference; support mismatch has probability tending to zero and is retained explicitly in the proofs. Unknown independent censoring is covered pointwise under its separate quotient-event product-rate, common-support, influence-stability, residual, and moment hypotheses. A smooth law proves that a two-time schedule strictly beats early-only and horizon-only inspection without claiming that pair is the continuous oracle.
gap: Existing results separately cover nonparametric monitoring design, labeled current-status competing-risk CIF estimation, fixed-law fusion of right-censored and current-status survival data, and parametric competing-risk trial design. No verified result supplies the cause-blind marked two-arm mixed-source efficiency operator together with continuous inspection-law optimization, computable global certificates, pilot selection, and conditional attainment under a known censoring randomization law.
fill: The proposed known-censoring theorems derive that functional, certify its global minimizer, delimit its support geometry, approximate it with auditable finite calculations, and turn it into a prospective two-stage estimator and interval. A uniform expansion over the pilot atomic class separates oracle-value consistency from root-\(n\) inference and states the histogram and numerical rates explicitly. The ordinary unknown-censoring tangent problem is stated separately rather than absorbed into the oracle claim.
